title: CRLR/427/2022 of ANJAR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 427 of 2022
Anjar ....Revisionist
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and Another ..... Respondents
Mr. Ahrar Baig, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. Lalit Miglani, A.G.A. with Ms. Sonika Khulbe, Brief Holder for the
State of Uttarakhand.

JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The challenge in this revision is made to
the order dated 18.06.2022, passed in Misc. Case No. 12
of 2018, Smt. Riwana Vs. Anjar, by the Family Court,
Kashipur, District Udham Singh Nagar ("the case").
2. Heard learned counsel for the revisionist
and perused the record.
3. It appears that the private respondent filed
an application seeking maintenance from the revisionist
under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973. According to the private respondent, the
revisionist befriended her and in the month of May,
2018, called her in a hotel room, spiked her drinks and
in an unconscious state, raped her. He also took
obscene photographs and videos of that incident. This

2
act was repeatedly done by the revisionist. He also
demanded money from the private respondent. He
threatened the private respondent to life in case she
reveals the incident to anyone. On 10.09.2018, the
private respondent gave a report at Police Station:-
Kashipur. When police contacted the revisionist, he
agreed to marry the private respondent. On 16.09.2018,
according to the private respondent, she and the
revisionist were married. But, after marriage, according
to the private respondent, the revisionist did not take
her with him. He would visit her in her father's house.
She was subsequently told that the marriage was
solemnized so as to avoid the case of rape against the
revisionist. It is the case of the private respondent that
subsequently the revisionist was harassed, tortured for
demand of money, etc. She is not able to maintain
herself, whereas, the revisionist earns Rs. 50,000/- from
different sources.
4. The revisionist filed his objections.
According to the revisionist, he and the private
respondent were speaking to each other; a false report
against the revisionist was filed by the private
respondent; the revisionist was pressurized to marry the
private respondent; under such circumstances, he and

3
the private respondent married on 16.09.2018, but the
private respondent was not sent with the revisionist.
According to the revisionist, thereafter, money was
demanded from him; the private respondent never joined
his company; they never established marital relations.
The revisionist has also objected that the private
respondent is able to maintain herself.
5. Parties adduced evidence in the case. After
hearing the parties, by the impugned judgment and
order, the revisionist has been directed to pay Rs.
4,000/- per month to the private respondent. Aggrieved
by it, the instant revision.
6. Learned counsel for the revisionist would
submit that in the instant case, it has not been
established that the private respondent is the married
wife of the revisionist.
7. Learned counsel for the revisionist would
submit that, although, the marriage ceremony took place
between the revisionist and the private respondent on
16.09.2018, but he would submit that the private
respondent never joined the company of the revisionist

4
and she did not discharge her marital obligations,
therefore, she is not entitled for maintenance.
8. This is a revision. The scope is much
restricted to the extent of examining the correctness,
legality and propriety of the impugned judgment and
order. Evaluation of evidence, at this stage, may not
generally be done, unless the finding is perverse or
irrelevant material is considered or relevant material is
left from consideration.
9. The argument, which is being raised in the
case, was also raised in the court below on behalf of the
revisionist. The court below has discussed it in quite
detail. The nikah between the revisionist and the private
respondent is admitted. What is the case of the
revisionist is that the private respondent never joined his
company.
10. On the other hand, it is the case of the
private respondent that the revisionist did not take her
after nikah. He used to visit her in her father's house.
11. It is admitted by the revisionist that then a
case was lodged against him. Thereafter, he was

5
compelled to marry the private respondent. It is the
categorical case of the private respondent that the
revisionist had raped her in the past. When the FIR was
lodged, the revisionist agreed to marry. Having
considered all these facts, the court below recorded a
finding that the relationship between the revisionist and
the private respondent is that of husband and wife.
12. This finding is not perverse. It is based on
evidence. It does not warrant any interference. No other
issue is raised. Hence, there is no reason to make any
interference in the impugned judgment and order.
Accordingly, the revision deserves to be dismissed at the
stage of admission itself.
13. The revision is dismissed in limine.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 09.09.2022
